Topics · Hard times

Is an earthquake a punishment from God?

No one can say why a particular disaster struck particular people; the Quran warns against claiming it. A word for the bereaved, a task for others.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

﴿قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْغَيْبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۚ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Quran · An-Naml 27:65

Translation

The secret things belong to Yahweh our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.

Original · Hebrew

הַ֨נִּסְתָּרֹ֔ת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהַנִּגְלֹ֞ת לָ֤ׄנׄוּׄ וּׄלְׄבָׄנֵׄ֨יׄנׄוּׄ֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 29:29

World English Bible

After every disaster, someone says it was a punishment. Ask how anyone could know. One verse says not to pursue what you have no knowledge of; the other, that no one but God knows the unseen. So to stand on a ruin and name the reason is to claim what no living person has. The same ground opens under the kind and the cruel, the infant and the old. No one has been told why it struck where it did.

A question for you

When people explain a disaster as a punishment, what do you notice?

If you sayThey are afraid, and want it to make sense.
ThenPerhaps. A world with a reason can feel safer than one without. That does not make their reason known.
If you sayIt is cruel to those who lost someone.
ThenIt adds a second wound to the first. The rule about knowledge speaks to that.
If you sayI have wondered it myself.
ThenMany have, especially after fear. Wondering is not the same as claiming to know.

Part 2 of 3

﴿مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَمَن يُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُۥ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

No disaster strikes except by permission of Allāh. And whoever believes in Allāh - He will guide his heart. And Allāh is Knowing of all things.

Quran · At-Taghabun 64:11

How happy is man in this his power that hath been granted unto him: that he needs not do anything but what God shall approve, and that he may embrace contentedly, whatsoever God doth send unto him?

Stoic writings · Meditations 12.8

Marcus Aurelius, Meditations (Casaubon, 1634)

﴿مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِى كِتَـٰبٍ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّبْرَأَهَآ ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ٢٢ لِّكَيْلَا تَأْسَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا تَفْرَحُوا۟ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ٢٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register[1634] before We bring it into being - indeed that, for Allāh, is easy - In order that you not despair over what has eluded you and not exult [in pride] over what He has given you. And Allāh does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful -

Translator's notes

[1634] i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

Quran · Al-Hadid 57:22-23

And dost thou that hast received all from another’s hands, repine and blame the Giver, if He takes anything from thee? Why, who art thou, and to what end comest thou here? was it not He that made the Light manifest unto thee, that gave thee fellow-workers, and senses, and the power to reason? And how brought He thee into the world? Was it not as one born to die; as one bound to live out his earthly life in some small tabernacle of flesh; to behold His administration, and for a little while share with Him in the mighty march of this great Festival Procession? Now therefore that thou hast beheld, while it was permitted thee, the Solemn Feast and Assembly, wilt thou not cheerfully depart, when He summons thee forth, with adoration and thanksgiving for what thou hast seen and heard?—“Nay, but I would fain have stayed longer at the Festival.”—Ah, so would the mystics fain have the rites prolonged; so perchance would the crowd at the Great Games fain behold more wrestlers still. But the Solemn Assembly is over! Come forth, depart with thanksgiving and modesty—give place to others that must come into being even as thyself.

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 139

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

The book does not say the earth moves outside God's knowledge. No calamity comes except by His leave, it says, and it was known before it came. That sharpens the question: if He permits it, why? These verses give steadiness, not an explanation: a heart steadied, so that a person is not destroyed by what they lost, nor swollen by what they were given. The Quran speaks in general of trial and reminder (2:155, 21:35), but tells no one why a particular day came to particular people.

A question for you

Which of these is hardest for you to hold?

If you sayThat God knew and allowed it.
ThenThat is the hard centre of the matter, and no complete answer is known. You are not asked to resolve it.
If you sayThat nature could be so blind.
ThenThen the question is whether blind forces are all there is. The book says they are not, and does not claim that removes the pain.
If you sayThat no one is at fault, so there is no one to be angry with.
ThenAnger with no address is very heavy. You may bring it here.

Original · Hebrew

Proverbs · 24:11

World English Bible

So what does the Quran give for such a day? Two things, and neither is a theory. For those struck, a sentence to say: we belong to God, and to Him we return. It explains nothing. It says where the dead have gone, and where we are going. For everyone else, a task: whoever saves one life, it is as if they saved all people. The weight of these verses falls on the next hour, on the hands in the rubble. Those who dig are doing what this verse honours.

A question for you

If you stood in such a place tomorrow, what would you most want to bring?

If you sayMy hands.
ThenThat is what the verse honours.
If you saySomeone to sit with those who lost people.
ThenThat may be the rarest thing to bring, and among the most needed.
If you sayAn answer.
ThenMany come wanting that. This page has no complete answer, and it will not pretend otherwise.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.
